candidates.title: ✅ The PERFECT Smith Machine Squat
candidates.description:
✅ The PERFECT Smith Machine Squat

Hand Placement:
Position your hands as close to your shoulders as your mobility comfortably allows. Pull the bar into your traps and squeeze your shoulder blades together to create strong upper back tension. Avoid placing your hands too far apart, as this reduces upper body tightness.

Forearm Position:
Angle your forearms so they are close to vertical, with elbows slightly pointing back. This supports proper bar positioning for a high-bar or mid-bar setup. Avoid flaring your elbows too far back, as it can compromise shoulder and wrist alignment.

Stance Width:
Stand about hip-width apart or slightly wider, depending on your individual anatomy, to optimize squat strength and depth. Avoid going too narrow or excessively wide, as this can limit power and mobility.

candidates.description:
I know what you’re thinking: “wait, I thought only training noobs use the smith machine for squats?” WRONG. In all reality, yes, the free weight barbell back squat is the king of lower body strength & hypertrophy developers. There’s no contesting that whatsoever.

However, for those of you looking to maximize hypertrophy by adding in some strong accessory work for quadriceps, the feet-forward smith squats are BOMB.

Simple, yet effective & consistent use of exercises like this will undoubtedly be of benefit to your hypertrophy training. However, if you can’t barbell squat 315 ATG, then this movement shouldn’t even be in your vocabulary yet.

candidates.title: Smith Machine Squat Variation - Quads vs Glutes
candidates.description:
Smith Machine Squat Variation – Targeting Quads vs Glutes

The Smith machine squat activates all the major leg muscles, but how you position your feet can shift the focus.
Heels elevated: Emphasizes the quads by increasing knee travel forward.
Toes elevated: Shifts the load to the glutes by encouraging more hip hinge and posterior chain engagement.
